critical.issue: REGRESSION (fixed by testing agent): @router.put('/profile') decorator had been deleted in routers/restaurants.py (my_restaurant's `return d` was directly followed by `async def update_profile`), so the route returned 404 and dashboard Profile save was broken. Decorator restored; verified non-404 live.

minor.issue: Spurious 409 'limit reached' when several orders arrive concurrently and no order_usage doc exists yet for the month (first order(s) of every month on Free). find_one_and_update upsert with filter {_id, count:{$lt:limit}} is NOT auto-retried by MongoDB on DuplicateKeyError (predicate isn't pure equality), so the losing upsert raises DuplicateKeyError which is mapped to 409. Reproduced live (1 of 8 concurrent orders rejected, ~1 in 4 runs) and in-process (1 of 500 reservations across runs). Fix: on DuplicateKeyError retry the find_one_and_update once without upsert (if it returns None -> real limit -> 409), or pre-upsert {$setOnInsert:{count:0}} by _id then do a non-upsert conditional $inc.

When no whopMembershipId is linked, the loop returns on the FIRST list_memberships entry whose metadata matches, even if that one is canceled/foreign-plan; a later active membership for the same restaurant is never considered. Prefer memberships with PRO_STATUSES (or iterate until applied:pro).

If apply_membership raises anything other than WhopError (e.g. DuplicateKeyError from the one_restaurant_per_membership index, or a DB error) the whop_events claim stays status 'processing' and the request 500s; Whop retries are then answered {duplicate:true} and the event is never processed. Wrap in generic except -> delete claim (or mark failed) and return 5xx.

Index creation for deletion_requests one_pending_per_restaurant and staff_invitations (TTL expires_at, restaurantId, email) is placed INSIDE _migrate_legacy_plans after the early return, so these indexes are only created on the very first startup with the migration. Works on this DB (already exist), but on any new environment where the migration doc is pre-present/copied they would never be created. Move them back to ensure_indexes.
Archived restaurants (deletedAt set, e.g. 'Sushi To Home') were not marked legacy; if an admin restores one it becomes Free (20 products / 30 orders / no staff/delivery). Confirm this is intended.

rca of the issue: First-of-month race: two concurrent reserve_order_slot calls both miss the (non-existent) usage doc; both attempt upsert-insert with _id '<rid>:<YYYY-MM>'; one wins, the other gets E11000. MongoDB only auto-retries upserts on duplicate key when the query is equality-only on the unique key; here the query contains count:{$lt:30}, so no retry and the code treats DuplicateKeyError as 'limit reached' -> 409. Repro: delete db.order_usage doc for a Free restaurant and fire 8-10 concurrent pickup orders; occasionally 1 returns 409 while count < 30. Mitigation: catch DuplicateKeyError, retry find_one_and_update with upsert=False; None => genuine limit. Profile regression: decorator line removed when /me was edited to add plan; restored.
